items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I mean Duke Ellington would tell you in a minute, “Yeah I stole that from Tchaikovsky, and I took that from Fats Waller...”

ctx.x: He’s got some formula that apparently appeals to some people.

That he took from Grover Washington of course. I mean Grover is the one that really is the inspiration for Kenny G. If he would just say that, that would make me, then I would get off my high horse. I mean really say well the boy, no matter what he’s doing at least he’s honest about where he’s stealing it from. I mean Duke Ellington would tell you in a minute, “Yeah I stole that from Tchaikovsky, and I took that from Fats Waller and I took this— and I just heard this somewhere, I probably stole it from somewhere…
know where he got it from.” But you know, as Duke used to say, good composers borrow, the best composers steal. The way it is.
